STYLE GUIDE
YOKAI FIGHTERS STYLE GUIDE: STAGE BACKDROPS

LOOK
L1. Toon-shaded game art: flat cel colour in 2-3 tone steps per surface, with a clean ink-brush outline of even weight. Shapes are simple and read at 720p. (Source: rules.md V1; style.md Style block)
L2. Matte surfaces and soft even lighting: no cast shadows, gloss, metallic sheen, rim light, baked ambient occlusion, bloom or glowing particles. A lantern's glow is a flat orange fill, never a bloom. (Source: style.md Style block and Negative prompt; Astra brief, Rules for every output; lantern-riverbank.md Palette)
L3. No photographic, PBR or painterly texture: no film grain, painterly brush noise, gritty detail, depth-of-field blur or volumetric light. The game adds its own toon shader and outline, so baked rendering is a RETAKE. (Source: rules.md V1; style.md Shared 3D settings; Astra brief, Rules for every output)
L4. It matches the accepted bamboo grove backdrop (the REFERENCE image) in outline weight, flatness and level of detail, so the stages read as one game. (Source: style.md Acceptance checklist 2; snowbound-shrine-gate.md Acceptance criteria)

PALETTE AND LORE
P1. Colours come from the muted ukiyo-e palette in style.md: indigo #2D3A5E, ink #1D1B21, persimmon #D8632C, rice paper #F1E8D4, pine #34483B, foxfire #F2A23A, shrine red #B5332B, brass #B08A48, snow shade #A9B4C8, water teal #3E7F86, brown #6E5A48, spring pink #E8A6B0 and the wood and straw tones. No neon, saturated primaries, hot pink or turquoise, and snow is never pure white. (Source: rules.md V1; style.md Palette; snowbound-shrine-gate.md Palette)
P2. Each stage shows its own place and hour: the Oni's snowbound mountain shrine gate at blue dusk (a shrine-red gate with a straw rope, snow-laden pines, indigo ridges); the Kappa's river at deep indigo night with paper lanterns drifting on dark water and reeds; the Tanuki's lamplit tea house (wooden beams, tatami, a row of tall blank paper screens); the Kitsune's bamboo grove at dusk. (Source: rules.md V9; vault Art-and-Audio#Stages; the three stage specs, Stage mood)
P3. The world is one rural Japanese province at the end of autumn. No modern objects, cities, castles, neon signs or tropical scenery; spring colour appears only on the tea house's season screens. (Source: GDD §2.1; vault Tone#The tone line, Story#The illusion loop; tanuki-tea-house.md Palette)
P4. Mischievous folklore with a melancholy edge, never horror: no skulls, blood, menacing faces, ruins or dread. Quiet, lantern-lit and a little lonely. (Source: rules.md S1 (tone applies to the whole game); vault Tone#The tone line)

S1. A stage backdrop is a wide 16:9 landscape image, full-bleed to the edges: no border, frame, vignette, letterbox or rounded corners. (Source: the three stage specs, Backdrop (S1) prompt and Acceptance criteria ("no letterbox after crop"))

S3. No text of any kind: no title, letters, kanji, logo, signature or watermark. (Source: style.md Negative prompt; stage specs Acceptance criteria)
S4. The lower third is calm, empty and low-contrast, because that is the band the fighters stand in; detail sits in the upper two thirds and the edges. (Source: the three stage specs, Backdrop (S1) prompt ("empty and uncluttered in the lower third") and Acceptance criteria)
